newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen range-bound after BOJ comments.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen range-bound after BOJ comments.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to be range-bound in a familiar band on Tuesday, and to have little effect from comments by the Bank of Japan's branch managers.

"JGBs are likely to be range-bound. The BOJ branch managers' views on the economy are becoming gradually stronger, but the market has already factored in their slightly bullish outlook," said a trader for a trust bank's securities unit.
Some will focus on June Tokyo department store sales data due at 2.30 p.m. (0530 GMT), traders said, adding the market will keep close watch on moves in share prices.
Although comments by BOJ branch managers' are unlikely to have much impact on the market overall, they may cap the upside of JGBs somewhat, a trust bank trader said.
"The comments are not enough to trigger selling of JGBs, but they may make the upside heavy," he said.
Eiichiro Kinoshita, the BOJ's Osaka branch manager, said on Monday that a slower recovery in Japan's non-manufacturing sector and by smaller firms will not affect the overall economic recovery.
The first trader said some selling might occur if June Tokyo department store sales were to show a year-on-year rise.
"If department store sales begin increasing again, it may lead to a view that the effect of the consumption tax on the economy has dissipated, and trigger selling of JGBs," the trader said.
In May, Tokyo department store sales fell 5.9 percent year-on-year.
The second trader said he felt there would be little impact from economic indicators to be released on Tuesday, and that the market's main concern will be movements in Tokyo share prices.
